title: Adic compactification cohomology and extension-by-zero sections
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ a quasi-compact open immersion, and $a_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the structure map [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $W=U,T$ put $B_W=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_W$, $E_W=B_W[1/\varpi]$. Use exactly the derived-complete integral, raw rationalized and common-finite-stage categories of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], their constructible hearts [def-weil-constructible-heart], and the continuous rational realization $J_W$ of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization].

For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Omega$, adic extension by zero, i.e. the rational/common-stage compact-support direct image of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] along $j$ computed with the compactification $(j,\mathrm{id}_T)$, gives an exact functor $j_!:\Sh_c(U,\Lambda)\to\Sh_c(T,\Lambda)$. At a common finite field its realization is the sheafification of the extension-by-zero module presheaf with continuous coefficient sheaf $E_T$, rather than discrete non-torsion coefficients on the etale site. There is a canonical identification $j^*j_!F\cong F$; the adic geometric fibre of $j_!F$ is zero at every point outside $U$, and is the fibre of $F$ inside $U$. These identifications use the fibres of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres].

If $T$ is proper over $k$, the compactification $a_U=(T\to\operatorname{Spec}k)\circ j$ gives natural linear isomorphisms
$$H_c^0(U,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh_c(T,\Lambda)}(\mathbf1_T,j_!F),\qquad H^0(U,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh_c(U,\Lambda)}(\mathbf1_U,F).$$
Under these identifications the compact-to-ordinary cohomology comparison is restriction of the displayed morphism along $j$, followed by $j^*j_!F\cong F$. All comparisons are natural in $F$, preserve coefficient units, and commute with restriction of ordinary sections to open subschemes and finite coefficient-field extension. At $\Omega$ objects, morphisms and these comparisons are computed at a common finite field and then extended as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. No injectivity or assertion about support of a section is included.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15 (continuous-coefficient realization and ambient six functors); Proposition 6.8.11(3) (integral cohomological constructibility). The compactification and degree-zero Hom normalization is an agent-formulated consequence, also using Milne Proposition 18.3(b), Definition 18.1. This is the open-extension and compactification comparison obligation, not a literal quotation of one proposition.

proof.text: Work first at a finite field $E$. The schemes $U,T,s$ satisfy the realization hypotheses: $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian (the only ideals of $k$ are $0,k$), and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies to their structure maps. Applying [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] over the one-point quasi-compact base $s$ bounds their dimensions, since the unique fibre is the scheme itself. Distinguish ordinary ringed-site extension $e_j$ for $B$-modules from the adic functor defined by the quotient tower. For an integral representative $K$, the compactification $(j,\mathrm{id}_T)$ in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] gives $Rj_!K=\mathcal L_TJ_j\mathcal R_UK$. Here the identity proper direct image is the identity and $J_j$ is termwise finite-level extension. Apply [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]: its specified system isomorphism $r_j(K):\mathcal R_T(e_jK)\cong J_j\mathcal R_UK$ respects every quotient transition, $e_jK$ is complete, and its map $d_j(K)$ identifies this very total limit with $e_jK$. Thus the adic and ordinary integral extensions agree naturally, with the stated open-adjunction normalization. This uses the strict-system isomorphism, rather than an inference that arbitrary maps agreeing at every finite level agree in the derived category.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; integral reduction-system identification via Stacks Tag 0GL1 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor) and the cited strict open-reduction comparison

proof.text: The tensor comparison of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], applied on the $B$-ringed sites with $N=E_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$, gives $E_T\otimes^L_{B_T}e_jK\cong e_j(E_U\otimes^L_{B_U}K)$. The $E_T$-action is the balanced tensor action. Combine this with step 1 and the formula for $J$ in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] to obtain $J_TRj_!QK\cong e_jJ_UQK$. The open unit identifies its restriction to $U$ with the identity. Naturality for integral maps implies naturality for rational maps: a map $f/\varpi^n$ is sent on both sides to $\varpi^{-n}$ times the map for $f$. Hence this is an identification of the given rational functors. The ringed extension is sheafification of the extension-by-zero $E_T$-module presheaf, by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Thus the coefficients here are the continuous $E_T$ of the realization theorem.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; Stacks Tags 03DI (sites-modules.tex, lemma-extension-by-zero), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), 0GL1 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor)

proof.text: At the rational stage [sk-lem-sf-open-ctf] says that $Rj_!$ preserves $D^b_c$ and every cohomological interval, without imposing a numerical integral Tor interval. In particular it preserves the heart. Under the t-exact equivalences $J_U,J_T$, its restriction is the exact module extension in step 2; consequently $j_!:\Sh_c(U,E)\to\Sh_c(T,E)$ is exact. This does not assume that an arbitrary rational-heart representative is an integral sheaf with flat finite reductions.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; Proposition 6.8.14(2); blueprint main-20261015, sk-lem-sf-open-ctf, rational-coefficient clause

proof.text: Choose the closed complement $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ of $j$ with reduced scheme structure. The ringed open--closed identities of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] give $j^{-1}e_jJ_UF\cong J_UF$ and $i^{-1}e_jJ_UF=0$. Apply the inverse-image comparison and full faithfulness of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] to get $j^*j_!F\cong F$ and $i^*j_!F=0$ in the adic hearts. A geometric point inside $U$ factors through $j$, and one outside $U$ factors through $i$ (the ideal of $Z$ maps to zero in its residue field). The pullback/fibre identity of [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], applied respectively to $j$ and $i$, gives the claimed inside fibre and zero outside fibre. The scheme $Z$ is again separated finite type, so both pullback comparisons apply.

Now suppose $T$ proper, and put $b:T\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For an integral representative $K$, the compact-support definition gives $Ra_{U!}K=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nRb_{*,n}j_!K_n$. By step 1 the strict tower $\operatorname{Res}_nj_!K_n$ is the reduction tower of $e_jK$. The completed-coefficient direct-image comparison of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison], applied to $f=b$ and the derived-complete object $e_jK$ (its strict reduction system being $\mathcal R_T(e_jK)$), therefore identifies this expression with the ordinary completed-coefficient $Rb_*^B(e_jK)$; its $n$-th projection is $Rb_*^B$ of the reduction map followed by the coefficient-restriction comparison. The same object is $Rb_*(Rj_!K)$ by the tower definition of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. All identifications are maps of strict towers, including their projections. Rationalizing and using [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization] gives $Ra_{U!}F\cong Rb_*j_!F$ and its continuous realization $Rb_*^E(e_jJ_UF)$. The cohomology definition [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] now gives $H_c^0(U,F)\cong H^0(T,j_!F)$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; Stacks Tag 0A07 (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim); Milne Definition 18.1, pp. 118-119

proof.text: For any $C\in D^b_c(s,E)$, [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] and the definition [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] identify $\operatorname{Fib}_s\mathbf1_s$ with $E[0]$: the continuous coefficient normalization of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] gives $B_s(s)=C(|s|,A)=A$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1_s,C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(E)}(E[0],\operatorname{Fib}_sC)$. The latter is $H^0(\operatorname{Fib}_sC)$, with normalization evaluation on $1$: indeed maps from $E[0]$ are cycles, homotopies identify cycles differing by a boundary, and $E[0]$ is K-projective since a cycle $z$ in an acyclic vector-space complex is $dh$ and the map $1\mapsto h$ is its null homotopy. [lem-coef-kprojective-derived-hom-bijection] makes this computation in the homotopy category a computation in the derived category. These descriptions prove naturality and $E$-linearity, not merely an abstract vector-space isomorphism.

source.place: Point coefficient normalization of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point; elementary cycle evaluation with the cited K-projective localization bijection

proof.text: Apply step 6 to $C=Ra_{W*}M$ for $W=U$ or $T$ and $M$ in its constructible heart. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] its degree-zero fibre cohomology is $H^0(W,M)$. The adjunction identification of [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization], with the pullback comparison of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1_s,Ra_{W*}M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(La_W^*\mathbf1_s,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1_W,M)$. The last unit identification is multiplication $E_W\otimes_{a_W^{-1}E_s}a_W^{-1}E_s\cong E_W$. Both objects in the last Hom are in the heart, which is a full subcategory by [def-weil-constructible-heart]. This proves the ordinary isomorphism for $U$; combined with step 5 for $M=j_!F$ it proves the compact-support isomorphism for $T$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; degree-zero Hom and ordinary-adjunction consequence, with the specified direct-image comparison

proof.text: The compact-to-ordinary map for this compactification is $Rb_*j_!F\to Rb_*Rj_*F\cong Ra_{U*}F$, where $j_!F\to Rj_*F$ is the $j^*\dashv Rj_*$-adjunct of the open-unit inverse $j^*j_!F\cong F$. At finite level this is exactly the extension-to-direct-image comparison; step 1 identifies the realized open unit and counit, and the direct-image realization identifies the actual ordinary units and counits. The last isomorphism is the canonical ringed derived direct-image compositor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. On a morphism $t:\mathbf1_T\to j_!F$ the adjunction formula therefore gives $\mathbf1_U\cong j^*\mathbf1_T\xrightarrow{j^*t}j^*j_!F\cong F$. Thus steps 5--7 identify the specified comparison with restriction. For an open $V\subset U$, restricting this expression gives $(j^*t)|_V$ followed by the restricted open-unit inverse; the normalized open unit in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] is identity on sections. This proves compatibility with ordinary open restriction, without assuming that compact support itself restricts functorially to every open.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; Milne Definition 18.1 and Proposition 18.3(b), pp. 118-121; canonical open-adjunction construction of the comparison

proof.text: For a finite extension $E\subset L$, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies completed scalar extension with ordinary derived coefficient tensor. Apply [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] with the new coefficient sheaf to obtain its open-extension comparison; on restriction to $U$ it is identity. The realization comparisons commute with this coefficient extension by [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] and [lem-a1-rational-direct-image-realization]. The actual ordinary-adjunction bijections commute with it by [lem-pur-ordinary-adjunction-scalar-compatibility], and point evaluation commutes with it by [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]. Thus each arrow of steps 5--8, including the restriction formula, commutes with scalar extension. Its unit normalization is $1\mapsto1$, $x\otimes1\mapsto x$, and $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto x\otimes ab$; no assertion that $j_!\mathbf1_U=\mathbf1_T$ is needed. Finally use [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]: represent $F$, a morphism, or a finite comparison diagram over one common finite field, apply the preceding formulas there, and pass to the common-stage class. Two representatives agree at a further finite extension, where the same scalar compatibility identifies the formulas. Inverses and compositions pass in the same way. By [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], standard cohomology and truncation are computed at a common finite stage; applying these to the finite-stage cone of a represented heart morphism shows that its kernel and cokernel, and hence exactness of $j_!$, are also computed stagewise. This proves the heart and fibre assertions as well as the comparison assertions at $\Omega$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1),(2), Lemma 6.8.2(1), Remark 6.8.15; specified common-finite-stage construction and scalar-normalized ordinary adjunction
